title: Polynomial-time computability of stored counts
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $i$ be a movement-count coordinate, and let $t$ be a natural-number-valued function on Boolean words. If the unary word of length $t(z)$ is polynomial-time computable as a function of $z$, then the unary word whose length is the stored movement count at time $t(z)$ is also polynomial-time computable as a function of $z$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
$t$ maps Boolean words to natural numbers
replaced: For every counter coordinate and polynomial-time unary time producer, the unary word of the stored movement count at the produced time is polynomial-time computable; projections, clock construction, repeated field scans, and decoding calls are all charged.
